reading.body:
Alexandria Paolozzi Moore is named on six AI lobbying filings, all for one client, FDD ACTION, and all naming bills from 2025 or later.

The pattern is narrow and deep. Six filings, one client, one firm, and fourteen distinct bills across the House and Senate. This is not a lobbyist spread across many AI clients. It is a single client relationship that touches a wide set of legislation, which is what an active policy shop looks like in disclosure data rather than what a diversified practice looks like.

The disclosed prior government position is an internship in the office of Representative Bill Posey in 2010. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires covered positions held in the prior twenty years to be listed, so its presence is a compliance fact, not evidence of influence. The filings also record a lobbyist id of 152507, and the data notes a different lobbyist shares the same name.

What this does not cover is substance. The data names bills and counts filings. It does not say what was lobbied for, what any bill would do, whether any bill moved, or what share of the client's AI work this represents. It also says nothing about compute, data centers, or power, so no claim about the grid can be drawn from it. The record shows who filed, for whom, and on which bills, and stops there.

summary: Alexandria Paolozzi Moore is named as a lobbyist on 6 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 152507. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
